question.text: Dividend income (IDCW) from mutual funds is taxed in the hands of the investor at:

answer.text: The investor's income tax slab rate

explanation.text: The Logic: Following the abolition of the Dividend Distribution Tax (DDT) at the fund level with effect from 1 April 2020 (FY 2020-21 onwards), mutual fund distributions paid under the Income Distribution cum Capital Withdrawal (IDCW) option are taxed in the hands of the investor. The distributed amount is added to the investor's total income and taxed at the investor's applicable income-tax slab rate. The fund/AMC also deducts tax at source on such payouts where the prescribed threshold and rate apply. The Trap: 10% and 15% flat-rate options reflect old DDT-era or special-rate frameworks and are not how investor-side IDCW is taxed. IDCW is also clearly not exempt from tax under the current regime. Note: The specific investor-slab taxation of IDCW (and associated TDS) is not stated on the cited pages of the NISM-Series-X-A Investment Adviser (Level 1) workbook, which on the pages checked defines IDCW vs growth options and discusses pre-tax / post-tax return concepts rather than the post-2020 IDCW tax mechanism. The framing above is general post-FY 2020-21 Indian income-tax knowledge.
